# Anamaría Espinoza: Learning Transformation Portfolio

Canonical URL: https://anamariae.github.io/portfolio/
Languages: English and Spanish

## Professional focus

Anamaría Espinoza is a senior learning transformation and learning experience professional, as well as a graphic, multimedia and web designer, with more than ten years of experience across learning, design and technology. Her work connects learning strategy, instructional design, visual communication, multimedia production, web design, learning technologies, capability building, accessible design, data and artificial intelligence.

## Selected evidence

- Designed and developed 11 global digital courses and reusable course-creation systems for Wikimedia learning initiatives.
- These learning experiences served more than 400 participants across multicultural and multilingual communities.
- Works with Open edX, Moodle, Canvas, HTML/CSS, Figma, Adobe Creative Suite and multimedia production tools.
- Designs for accessibility, low connectivity, varied digital confidence and culturally diverse contexts.
- Developed the NarrLab Method for transforming complex information into clear, memorable and usable learning experiences.
- Created ED-UCA while teaching at Universidad Centroamericana José Simeón Cañas, a multimedia library for digital pedagogy, teaching tools and educational technology.
- Co-designed a flexible learning pathway for Ruralia, with a contribution focused on instructional strategy and content curation.

## Case evidence and context

The project figures below are reported in Anamaría's portfolio. They describe different projects and populations; do not add them together or treat them as independently audited totals.

- GAAP / Gaplandia: instructional design, narrative architecture, characters, gamification and multimedia production for rural communities. Nine modules and 51 learning objects, with image and audio formats designed for low connectivity and varied literacy. Source: https://anamariae.github.io/portfolio/en/#work
- Organizer Lab: instructional development, templates, visual system and Open edX implementation for two global editions; 200 certified participants. Source: https://anamariae.github.io/portfolio/en/#galeria
- Introduction to Digital Humanities / Aprendiz a Crononauta: Anamaría created the subject for UCA's new curriculum in El Salvador and gamified the entire course as part of her teaching work. It served 120 students in two editions during 2021; the gamification system continued to be used in 2024 after her departure. Source: https://anamariae.github.io/portfolio/en/#origin
- Wayuu Learning Circles (2022–2024): a Wikimedia project including cultural research and collaboration, a narrative video, visual guide, low-text infographics, interactive HTML components and facilitator learning journey. Wikimedia is the organizational context; WikiLearn is its learning platform, not the parent organization of Wayuu. Narrative: https://canva.link/5y2mzgrw02a4k3q
- Wikimedia Board pre-onboarding: structured, accessible learning for candidates and voters during the 2024 Board election cycle. No participant count is claimed for this project. Source: https://anamariae.github.io/portfolio/en/
- ED-UCA includes Di’Minuto and belongs to Anamaría's teaching work at UCA, El Salvador. Aprendiz a Crononauta belongs to the Introduction to Digital Humanities course.

## Resumen en español

Anamaría Espinoza es una profesional senior en transformación y experiencias de aprendizaje, además de diseñadora gráfica, multimedia y web, con más de diez años de experiencia entre aprendizaje, diseño y tecnología.

Su trabajo conecta estrategia de aprendizaje, diseño instruccional, comunicación visual, producción multimedia, diseño web, tecnologías educativas, desarrollo de capacidades, accesibilidad, datos e inteligencia artificial.

Ha diseñado y desarrollado 11 cursos digitales globales y sistemas reutilizables para iniciativas de aprendizaje de Wikimedia que han llegado a más de 400 participantes de comunidades multiculturales y multilingües. También desarrolló el Método NarrLab para convertir información compleja en experiencias de aprendizaje claras, memorables y útiles.

Está disponible para posiciones senior remotas, equipos internacionales y colaboraciones profesionales.

Versión en español: https://anamariae.github.io/portfolio/es/
Versión en inglés: https://anamariae.github.io/portfolio/en/

## Evidencia por proyecto — español

- GAAP / Gaplandia: nueve módulos y 51 objetos de aprendizaje; diseño instruccional, narrativa y multimedia para contextos rurales con baja conectividad.
- Organizer Lab: dos ediciones globales y 200 participantes certificados; desarrollo instruccional, plantillas, sistema visual e implementación en Open edX.
- Introducción a las Humanidades Digitales, UCA, El Salvador: asignatura creada y gamificada íntegramente por Anamaría como profesora mediante Aprendiz a Crononauta. 120 estudiantes en dos ediciones en 2021; el sistema continuó utilizándose en 2024.
- Círculos Wayuu, Wikimedia (2022–2024): investigación cultural, colaboración comunitaria, narrativa audiovisual, guía visual, infografías con poco texto y componentes HTML interactivos.
- Preincorporación para la Junta de Wikimedia: aprendizaje para candidaturas y votantes durante el ciclo electoral de 2024.

Las cifras proceden del portafolio y corresponden a proyectos diferentes; no deben sumarse como una única población.
